issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (abstract method messageOnFeed():String and task text describing String return values). In the solution repository, Animal.messageOnFeed() is declared to return FeedResponse (public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed()), introducing a different return type than the specification. This cross-artifact return-type mismatch will confuse students about the expected signature and what they must implement (String vs. FeedResponse).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String and update Pig/Seal implementations to return String (remove or stop using FeedResponse), or (B) if FeedResponse is intended, update the problem statement, UML, and template to specify messageOnFeed():FeedResponse and document how the FeedResponse is to be used/printed. Prefer option (A) to match the current exercise description and examples.

issues.description: The solution repository is internally inconsistent: Animal.messageOnFeed() is declared to return FeedResponse, Pig.messageOnFeed() and Seal.messageOnFeed() return FeedResponse objects, but Goat.messageOnFeed() returns a String. These differing return types within the solution code itself create a structural compilation error and make the solution unusable as a coherent reference implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Make all implementations and the abstract declaration consistent. Either (1) change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String and update Pig and Seal to return String (removing FeedResponse), or (2) change Goat.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse and ensure all implementations construct and return FeedResponse consistently. Additionally, ensure FeedResponse usage (if kept) is reflected in the exercise text and template so students are not surprised by the custom type.

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML/tasks) specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning a String (messageOnFeed():String). The solution repository implements messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (introducing a new class FeedResponse) and the subclasses (Seal, Pig) likewise return FeedResponse. This represents the same conceptual entity — the feed message returned by messageOnFeed() — but it is represented with a different type/name in the solution. Students following the problem and template will expect to implement messageOnFeed() returning a String; the solution's use of FeedResponse (and FeedResponse.toString()) is an unexpected, unmentioned indirection that creates cognitive mapping overhead and may confuse students about the required method signature and the intended return value.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change Animal.messageOnFeed() and all overriding implementations (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return a String (the feed message) instead of a FeedResponse object. Remove the FeedResponse type (or keep it only as an internal helper, but do not change the public method signature), and update places that call messageOnFeed() (e.g., Farm.feedAllAnimals and Farm.singFarmSongVerse) to handle the returned String. Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intentionally desired, update the problem statement and template to explicitly require/describe messageOnFeed() returning a FeedResponse and explain the purpose of that class so students are not surprised.
